'''Elizabeth M. Ward''' is an American scientist and researcher for the [[American Cancer Society]]. She received her [[PhD]] in [[Epidemiology]] from the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref name="AMC Bio" /> Ward serves as the National Vice President of Intramural Research for the [[American Cancer Society]] and Chair of the [[World Trade Center Health Program]] Scientific and Technical Advisory Committee.<ref name="AMC Bio">{{cite web|title=Elizabeth Ward, PhD|url=http://www.cancer.org/research/acsresearchers/elizabeth-ward-phd|website=American Cancer Society|publisher=American Cancer Society|accessdate=6 December 2016|archive-date=23 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160623142806/http://www.cancer.org/research/acsresearchers/elizabeth-ward-phd|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="World Trade Center Roster">{{cite web|title=WTC Health Program: Scientific/Technical Advisory Committee (STAC)|url=https://www.cdc.gov/wtc/stac_members.html|website=World Trade Center Health Program|publisher=World Trade Center Health Program|accessdate=6 December 2016|archive-date=20 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220115612/https://www.cdc.gov/wtc/stac_members.html|url-status=live}}</ref> She has held many positions in various cancer research organizations including a position on the [[National Cancer Institute]]'s Board of Scientific Counselors for Clinical Sciences and Epidemiology.<ref name="National Cancer Institute Roster">{{cite web|title=2013 Fact Book|url=https://www.cancer.gov/about-nci/budget/fact-book/archive/2013-fact-book.pdf|website=National Cancer Institute|publisher=National Cancer Institute|accessdate=6 December 2016|archive-date=30 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161230190142/https://www.cancer.gov/about-nci/budget/fact-book/archive/2013-fact-book.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> In recognition for her prominent work in the medical research field, she has received two different awards: U.S. [[Public Health Service Meritorious Service Medal]]<ref name="AMC Bio"/> and the Calum S. Muir Memorial Award.<ref name="Calum S. Muir Memorial Award">{{cite web |last1= |first1= |title=Calum S. Muir Memorial Award |url=https://www.naaccr.org/Membership/CalumSMuir.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220102534/https://www.naaccr.org/Membership/CalumSMuir.aspx |archive-date=20 December 2016 |accessdate=6 December 2016 |website=www.naaccr.org |publisher=NAACCR Inc.}}</ref> Ward's work is heavily centered around "cancer disparities, cancer treatment and outcomes, cancer surveillance, [[occupational cancer]] and environmental cancer."<ref name="Detailed AMC Bio" />

==Education==
Ward received her [[PhD]] in [[Epidemiology]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. Following that, she focused her studies on [[Occupational cancer]] with her work at the [[National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health]] (NIOSH) for 21 years.<ref name="AMC Bio" /> Ward has continued to focus her work on [[Epidemiology]] and Surveillance Research at the [[American Cancer Society]].<ref name="AMC Bio" />

==Career==
In 1995, Ward was appointed Chief of the Industry wide Studies Branch, Division of Surveillance, Hazard Evaluations and Field Studies of [[National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health]].<ref name="NIOSH ref">{{cite web|title=Oxford Journals: Monitoring of Aromatic Amine Exposures in Workers at a Chemical Plant With a Known Bladder Cancer Excess|url=http://jnci.oxfordjournals.org/content/88/15/1046.short|archive-url=https://archive.today/20161114200103/http://jnci.oxfordjournals.org/content/88/15/1046.short|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 November 2016|accessdate=6 December 2016}}</ref> She retired from this position in 2002, and later that year Ward joined the Department of Epidemiology and Surveillance Research at the American Cancer Society.<ref name="AMC Bio" /> It was here that she was responsible for directing the Surveillance Research group, which led her to her current position as National Vice President for Intramural Research.<ref name="AMC Bio" /> Ward has been largely involved in various cancer organizations. She has served as the co-chair for the National Coordinating Council for Cancer Surveillance and held a chair position for the Cancer Research Surveillance Committee.<ref name="Detailed AMC Bio">{{cite web|title=Elizabeth Ward, PhD|url=http://blogs.cancer.org/expertvoices/elizabeth-ward-phd/|website=AMC|publisher=American Cancer Society|accessdate=6 December 2016|archive-date=22 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161222130216/http://blogs.cancer.org/expertvoices/elizabeth-ward-phd/|url-status=live}}</ref> Ward has also operated as "the sponsoring member organization representative to the [[North American Association of Central Cancer Registries]]."<ref name="Detailed AMC Bio" /> Her involvement grew as she participated in advisory committees for the [[National Cancer Institute]]'s Shanghai Women's Study<ref name="Shanghai Women's Study Article">{{cite journal|title=Gliomas and Farm Pesticide Exposure in Women: The Upper Midwest Health Study|journal=Environmental Health Perspectives|date=May 2005|volume=5|issue=113|pages=546–551|pmc=1257545|pmid=15866761|vauthors=Carreón T, Butler MA, Ruder AM, Waters MA, Davis-King KE, Calvert GM, Schulte PA, Connally B, Ward EM, Sanderson WT, Heineman EF, Mandel JS, Morton RF, Reding DJ, Rosenman KD, Talaska G|doi=10.1289/ehp.7456}}</ref> and the Sister Study done by the [[National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences]].<ref name="Sister Study">{{cite web|title=Sister Study That Examines Causes of Breast Cancer Opens|url=http://www.news-medical.net/news/2004/10/18/5677.aspx|website=News-Medical.net|publisher=News Medical Life Sciences|accessdate=6 December 2016|date=18 October 2004|archive-date=20 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220075405/http://www.news-medical.net/news/2004/10/18/5677.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref>

Ward also spends time "regularly reviewing articles for occupational and environmental and cancer journals."<ref name="Detailed AMC Bio" /> She has been counted as an attendee of the Peer Review Panel for the [[National Toxicology Program]],<ref name="National Toxicology Program">{{cite web|title=National Toxicology Program|url=https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/sites/default/files/ntp/about_ntp/monopeerrvw/2013/december/peerreviewrpt20131213_508.pdf|publisher=National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences|access-date=6 December 2016|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202030253/https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/ntp/about_ntp/monopeerrvw/2013/december/peerreviewrpt20131213_508.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> as a participant on the Advisory Group for the [[International Agency for Research on Cancer]] Monograph program,<ref name="IARC">{{cite web|title=IARC Monographs on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans|url=https://monographs.iarc.fr/ENG/Publications/internrep/08-001.pdf|website=monographs.iarc.fr|publisher=World Health Organization International Agency for Research on Cancer|accessdate=6 December 2016|archive-date=17 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120617060818/http://monographs.iarc.fr/ENG/Publications/internrep/08-001.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> and has also took part on "expert committees" for the WHO [[International Programme on Chemical Safety]].<ref name="Detailed AMC Bio" />

Ward has been involved with research as well as in current events and concerns in the community. After the [[September 11 attacks|9/11]] attacks, Ward advocated a pro-active stance from the government on testing for cancer of relief workers, given the unique circumstances that existed and the large exposure to unknown hazards.<ref name="Sept 11 response">{{cite news|title=Experts say science lacking on 9/11, cancer ties|url=https://newspaperarchive.com/profile/susun-wilkinson/clipnumber/22011/|accessdate=15 November 2015|publisher=Daily Herald Suburban Chicago|date=9 July 2012|location=Chicago, Illinois|page=146|via=[[Newspaperarchive.com]]|archive-date=3 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231203232310/https://newspaperarchive.com/profile/anonymous-1012137/|url-status=live}} {{open access}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2002, Ward received the United States [[Public Health Service Meritorious Service Medal]] to recognize her "notable career"<ref name="AMC Bio" />

In 2012, Ward received the Calum S. Muir Memorial Award "for her enduring dedication to excellence in cancer surveillance, research, and cancer registration and her generous contributions of service and leadership to the NAACCR community."<ref name="Calum S. Muir Memorial Award" />
